title: Domain 5 extra questions (5.1-5.6)
note: Original questions written for IdentityOps Lab. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks.

questions.stem: A company documents how it will keep taking customer orders and paying staff during a long regional power outage, including alternate work locations and manual workarounds. Which of the following policies does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: A business continuity policy covers keeping essential business functions running during a disruption. A disaster recovery policy is narrower: it focuses on restoring IT systems and data after a disaster, not on how the business keeps operating.

questions.stem: A software company requires that security requirements be defined at the start of every project, that code be peer reviewed, and that security testing pass before any release. Which of the following policies sets these requirements?
questions.explanation: An SDLC policy governs how software is planned, built, tested and released, including security at each phase. Change management controls changes to production systems, but it does not define how the software itself is designed and tested.

questions.stem: Senior management approves a high-level document that states the organization's commitment to protecting information, assigns overall security responsibilities, and serves as the foundation for all other security documents. Which of the following is this document?
questions.explanation: The information security policy is the top-level statement of intent and responsibility that other policies, standards and procedures support. An acceptable use policy is narrower, covering only how users may use company systems.

questions.stem: A policy states that if the primary data center is lost, critical servers must be restored at the secondary site, and it names the executives who are authorized to order the switchover. Which of the following policies is this?
questions.explanation: A disaster recovery policy governs restoring IT systems after a major outage and who can invoke the plan. An incident response policy addresses security incidents such as breaches, not the relocation of systems after losing a facility.

questions.stem: Which of the following documents defines the authority, roles, and severity levels for handling security incidents across the organization, without listing the step-by-step technical actions for each type of attack?
questions.explanation: A policy sets direction, authority and responsibilities at a high level. A playbook is the tempting choice, but it contains the detailed, step-by-step actions for a specific type of incident.

questions.stem: The security team publishes a mandatory document that requires all passwords to be at least 14 characters, checked against a list of breached passwords, and locked after 10 failed attempts. Which of the following BEST describes this document?
questions.explanation: A standard sets specific, mandatory requirements that support a policy. A guideline would only recommend these settings, and this document makes them required.

questions.stem: A company requires that every data center door use a badge reader with anti-passback and that visitor logs be kept for one year. These requirements are mandatory at all sites. Which of the following BEST describes the document that contains them?
questions.explanation: Specific, mandatory technical and physical requirements belong in a standard. A procedure would describe the steps for carrying out a task, such as signing a visitor in, rather than set the required controls.

questions.stem: A mandatory document requires that access be granted by job role, that user access be reviewed every 90 days, and that administrators use separate privileged accounts. Which of the following does this document represent?
questions.explanation: These are specific, required rules for how access is managed, which makes the document a standard. The information security policy states high-level intent and would not list review intervals or account requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes the difference between a standard and a guideline?
choices: A standard is mandatory, while a guideline is a recommendation
A guideline is mandatory, while a standard is a recommendation
A standard gives step-by-step instructions, while a guideline sets intent
A guideline is approved by the board, while a standard is approved by IT
questions.answer: A standard is mandatory, while a guideline is a recommendation
questions.explanation: Standards set required, specific rules; guidelines offer advice that people are encouraged but not required to follow. Step-by-step instructions describe a procedure, not a standard.

questions.stem: On a new hire's first day, HR and IT must create accounts with role-based access, issue a laptop, collect a signed acceptable use agreement, and schedule security training. Which of the following ensures these steps happen the same way for every new employee?
questions.explanation: An onboarding procedure lists the repeatable steps for bringing a new person into the organization securely. Offboarding is the reverse process, removing access when someone leaves.

questions.stem: The help desk receives a document that lists, in order, the steps an analyst must take to verify a caller's identity before resetting a password. Which of the following types of document is this?
questions.explanation: A procedure is a set of ordered steps for performing a specific task. A standard defines what must be achieved, such as required verification methods, but not the sequence of actions to follow.

questions.stem: A company that operates only within one country must comply with a federal privacy law that applies to every business in that country. Which of the following external considerations does this law represent?
questions.explanation: A law that applies across a whole country is a national consideration. Local/regional considerations apply to a state, province or city, not to the entire country.

questions.stem: A retailer that has sold only in its home country begins shipping to customers in more than 20 countries and must account for the data protection laws of each. Which of the following external considerations is the retailer now facing?
questions.explanation: Operating across many countries brings global considerations, where multiple nations' laws apply. National would cover only the laws of the home country.

questions.stem: The company's attorneys warn that if customer data is exposed through weak security, customers could sue the company for negligence. Which of the following external considerations does this warning represent?
questions.explanation: Exposure to lawsuits and liability is a legal consideration. Regulatory considerations come from rules a government agency enforces, which is not what the attorneys describe here.

questions.stem: A government energy agency issues cybersecurity rules that all power utilities must follow, inspects utilities for compliance, and can impose penalties. Which of the following external considerations BEST describes these rules?
questions.explanation: Rules written and enforced by a government regulator are a regulatory consideration. Industry considerations come from industry bodies or contracts, such as card brand requirements, rather than a government agency.

questions.stem: A company forms a group of leaders from IT, legal, HR, and finance that meets monthly to set security priorities and approve new security policies. Which of the following governance structures is this?
questions.explanation: A cross-functional group that steers security decisions is a governance committee. The board of directors sits above management and is elected by shareholders, and it is not made up of department leaders.

questions.stem: At a company with offices in eight countries, a single security office at headquarters writes every security policy and must approve any policy change at the regional offices. Which of the following governance structures does this describe?
questions.explanation: Centralized governance keeps decision-making authority in one central body. In a decentralized structure, each region would make and enforce its own security decisions.

questions.stem: A business analyst in marketing is responsible for the quality of the customer data set, keeping its labels and definitions accurate, and making sure it is used in line with the data policy. Which of the following roles does the analyst hold?
questions.explanation: A data steward manages data quality, metadata and proper use on a day-to-day business level. A data controller is the tempting choice, but the controller decides the purposes and means of processing personal data rather than maintaining data quality.

questions.stem: A news report reveals a zero-day vulnerability in a popular VPN appliance. The risk team immediately assesses what the flaw means for the company's own VPN, outside its normal schedule. Which of the following types of risk assessment is this?
questions.explanation: An ad hoc assessment is performed as needed in response to an event. A recurring assessment happens on a fixed schedule, such as every year.

questions.stem: A company policy requires the risk team to repeat a full enterprise risk assessment during the first quarter of every year. Which of the following types of risk assessment does the policy require?
questions.explanation: An assessment repeated at a set interval is recurring. Continuous assessment would update risk in near real time with automated data rather than once a year.

questions.stem: Before acquiring a small competitor, a company assesses the risks of the competitor's network. The assessment will not be repeated, because the network will be shut down after the merger. Which of the following types of risk assessment is this?
questions.explanation: A one-time assessment is done for a specific project or decision and is not repeated. Ad hoc assessments respond to an unexpected event, such as a new vulnerability, rather than a planned single project.

questions.stem: A risk team interviews asset owners, reviews past incidents, and holds workshops to list the threats and vulnerabilities that could affect the company. No likelihood or impact ratings have been assigned yet. Which of the following activities is the team performing?
questions.explanation: Listing possible risks before rating them is risk identification. Risk analysis comes next and assigns likelihood and impact to each risk.

questions.stem: A warehouse is valued at $1,000,000. Analysts estimate that a fire would destroy 40% of the building's value. Which of the following terms describes the 40% figure?
questions.explanation: The exposure factor is the percentage of an asset's value lost in one event. Single loss expectancy is the dollar result of multiplying the asset value by the exposure factor, which here would be $400,000.

questions.stem: Stolen-laptop incidents cost a company about $10,000 each, and the company averages 3 of these incidents per year. Which of the following is the annualized loss expectancy for laptop theft?
questions.explanation: ALE equals SLE multiplied by ARO, so $10,000 x 3 = $30,000 per year. $10,000 is only the single loss expectancy for one incident.

questions.stem: Each entry in a company's risk register names a specific manager who is accountable for monitoring the risk and making sure the chosen treatment is carried out. Which of the following BEST describes this manager?
questions.explanation: The risk owner is accountable for managing a particular risk and its treatment. A data custodian protects data day to day but is not assigned accountability for risks in the register.

questions.stem: Which of the following documents lists an organization's identified risks along with their ratings, owners, chosen treatments, and current status?
questions.explanation: A risk register is the central record of identified risks and how they are being handled. A business impact analysis studies the effects of losing business functions, but it does not track every risk and its treatment.

questions.stem: A risk register states that any risk scored above 15 on a 25-point scale must be escalated to the CISO within 5 business days. Which of the following BEST describes the score of 15?
questions.explanation: A risk threshold is the level at which a risk triggers a required action, such as escalation. A key risk indicator is a metric that is tracked over time to warn that a risk is changing, not the cut-off point itself.

questions.stem: A hospital board states that it prefers stability and will avoid adopting new technologies until they have been proven elsewhere, accepting as little risk as possible. Which of the following BEST describes the hospital's risk appetite?
questions.explanation: A conservative risk appetite accepts minimal risk and favors stability. An expansionary appetite would accept more risk in pursuit of growth.

questions.stem: A mid-sized retailer's leadership says it will weigh each new opportunity on its merits, accepting moderate risk when benefits clearly justify it but not seeking out risk for growth. Which of the following BEST describes this risk appetite?
questions.explanation: A neutral appetite balances risk and reward without strongly favoring either. A conservative appetite would lean toward avoiding risk even when benefits are clear.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms refers to the overall amount and type of risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives?
questions.explanation: Risk appetite is the broad level of risk the organization is willing to take on. Risk tolerance is narrower: the acceptable variation around that appetite for a specific objective or measure.

questions.stem: A web application is vulnerable to SQL injection. The company deploys a web application firewall and fixes the input validation in the code to reduce the chance of a successful attack. Which of the following risk management strategies is the company using?
questions.explanation: Adding controls to reduce likelihood or impact is mitigation. Avoidance would mean removing the application or feature entirely so the risk no longer exists.

questions.stem: The cost of encrypting an old internal test server would far exceed the value of the data on it. Leadership documents the decision and takes no further action on the risk. Which of the following risk management strategies is this?
questions.explanation: Knowingly and formally deciding to live with a risk is acceptance. Transfer would shift the financial impact to another party, such as an insurer.

questions.stem: A shared lobby kiosk only displays a building map and never stores data, so it is formally and permanently released from the company's endpoint encryption requirement. Which of the following BEST describes this release?
questions.explanation: An exemption permanently releases something from a requirement because the requirement does not reasonably apply. An exception is a temporary, approved deviation from a requirement that still applies.

questions.stem: A business impact analysis finds that the payroll system must be back online within 8 hours of an outage to avoid missing pay deadlines. Which of the following metrics does the 8-hour value represent?
questions.explanation: RTO is the maximum time a system can be unavailable before it must be restored. RPO is the tempting choice, but it measures how much data can be lost, expressed as time since the last good backup.

questions.stem: A storage vendor states that its drives run for an average of 1.2 million hours before a failure occurs. Which of the following metrics is the vendor reporting?
questions.explanation: MTBF measures the average operating time between failures and indicates reliability. MTTR measures how long it takes to fix a component after it fails.

questions.stem: Before linking a supplier's ordering portal to its network, a company gets the supplier's permission and hires a firm to actively try to exploit weaknesses in the portal. Which of the following vendor assessment methods is this?
questions.explanation: Actively attempting to exploit a vendor's systems is penetration testing. A questionnaire only collects the vendor's own answers about its controls and does not test them.

questions.stem: A prospective vendor shares reports written by its own audit department that show how it checked its access controls and change management over the past year. Which of the following types of vendor assessment evidence is this?
questions.explanation: Reports produced by the vendor's own audit staff are evidence of internal audits. An independent assessment would be performed by an outside party with no stake in the outcome.

questions.stem: A company asks a software vendor for a software bill of materials and reviews the open-source libraries and upstream suppliers the product depends on. Which of the following is the company performing?
questions.explanation: Examining the components and suppliers behind a product is supply chain analysis. Penetration testing probes a running system for exploitable flaws rather than reviewing where its parts came from.

questions.stem: A company considering a new cloud backup provider hires an outside security firm, with no ties to either party, to evaluate the provider's controls. Which of the following BEST describes this evaluation?
questions.explanation: An evaluation by a third party with no stake in the result is an independent assessment. A self-assessment would be completed by the vendor about itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes due diligence when selecting a vendor?
choices: Monitoring the vendor's performance after onboarding
Applying ongoing controls to protect the data you share with it
Ending the relationship when the vendor fails an audit
Investigating the vendor's risks before signing an agreement
questions.answer: Investigating the vendor's risks before signing an agreement
questions.explanation: Due diligence is the research done before committing, such as checking finances, breaches and certifications. Ongoing protection of shared data is due care, which happens after the relationship begins.

questions.stem: During a vendor selection, it emerges that the consultant scoring the bids receives a referral commission from one of the vendors if it wins the contract. Which of the following issues does this create?
questions.explanation: A personal financial gain tied to one bidder creates a conflict of interest that can bias the selection. Collusion would involve the vendors secretly coordinating with each other, which is not described here.

questions.stem: An evaluator on a vendor selection panel discloses that her brother is a senior manager at one of the bidding firms. Which of the following should the panel do FIRST?
choices: Disqualify the vendor from the process
Ask her to sign a non-disclosure agreement
Continue and note the relationship later
Remove her from scoring that vendor's bid
questions.answer: Remove her from scoring that vendor's bid
questions.explanation: Recusing the conflicted evaluator protects the fairness of the selection without unfairly punishing the vendor. Disqualifying the vendor is an overreaction, since the vendor did nothing wrong by having an employee related to an evaluator.

questions.stem: A company is choosing between three cloud email providers. Which of the following is the PRIMARY security reason to perform due diligence on each provider before selection?
choices: To find risks a provider could introduce before committing
To negotiate a lower price for the email service over the contract term
To confirm the provider's uptime after go-live
To transfer liability for breaches to the provider
questions.answer: To find risks a provider could introduce before committing
questions.explanation: Due diligence surfaces security, financial and operational risks while the company can still choose another provider. Confirming uptime after go-live is vendor monitoring, which happens later.

questions.stem: Before sharing unreleased product designs with a potential manufacturing partner, a company wants the partner to agree in writing to keep the designs confidential. Which of the following agreements should be signed?
questions.explanation: A non-disclosure agreement legally obligates the parties to keep shared information confidential. An MOU records an intent to cooperate and usually does not create binding confidentiality obligations.

questions.stem: Two hospitals agree to share an ambulance dispatch system. They need a document that spells out each hospital's specific responsibilities in more detail than a statement of intent, but no payment changes hands. Which of the following BEST fits this need?
questions.explanation: A memorandum of agreement documents the specific responsibilities each party has agreed to and is more detailed than an MOU. An MOU only records general intent and goodwill without defined duties.

questions.stem: A company expects to hire the same security consulting firm for many projects over the next 3 years. It wants to agree on payment terms, liability, and confidentiality once, rather than for every project. Which of the following agreements should it sign?
questions.explanation: A master service agreement sets the general terms that govern all future work between the parties. A statement of work is then signed for each individual project to define its deliverables.

questions.stem: After onboarding a payment processor, a company subscribes to a service that alerts it to the processor's security rating changes and checks each year that the processor's audit report is still current. Which of the following is the company doing?
questions.explanation: Ongoing review of a vendor after the relationship starts is vendor monitoring. Due diligence happens before the agreement is signed.

questions.stem: A company sends each supplier the same standard form asking about encryption, access control, incident response, and employee training. Which of the following is the company using?
questions.explanation: A questionnaire gathers consistent information about each supplier's controls at scale. A right-to-audit clause gives the company permission to inspect a supplier, but it is a contract term, not a set of questions.

questions.stem: A vendor completed a security questionnaire stating that all laptops are encrypted and MFA is required for every account. Which of the following is the MAIN limitation of relying on these answers?
choices: The questions cannot cover technical controls
The questionnaire legally binds the company
The answers are self-reported and not verified
The answers expire as soon as they are submitted
questions.answer: The answers are self-reported and not verified
questions.explanation: Questionnaire responses are the vendor's own claims, so they should be backed by evidence such as audit reports or testing for higher-risk vendors. Questionnaires can and often do ask about technical controls such as encryption and MFA.

questions.stem: During an authorized penetration test, a tester discovers a vulnerable server at an IP address that is not listed in the agreed scope. Which of the following should the tester do?
choices: Exploit it to prove the risk to the client
Stop and contact the client before testing it
Scan it lightly since it is on the same network
Ignore it and leave it out of the report
questions.answer: Stop and contact the client before testing it
questions.explanation: Testing outside the agreed scope is unauthorized, so the tester should pause and get the client's direction. Exploiting the server, even with good intentions, breaks the rules of engagement.

questions.stem: A client wants penetration testers to avoid denial-of-service techniques and to stay away from social engineering of the executive team. Where should these restrictions be documented?
questions.explanation: The rules of engagement define what testers may and may not do, including prohibited techniques and targets. An NDA covers confidentiality of findings, not which techniques are allowed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY reason a penetration tester needs signed rules of engagement before starting work?
choices: It guarantees the tester will find every vulnerability
It gives written permission that separates testing from an attack
It sets the uptime the client must keep during the test
It replaces the need for a contract with the client
questions.answer: It gives written permission that separates testing from an attack
questions.explanation: Written authorization with defined scope protects both parties and shows the activity is legitimate testing. Rules of engagement do not replace the commercial contract, which still covers payment and liability.

questions.stem: A penetration test of a hospital must not disrupt patient care. Which of the following items is MOST important to include in the rules of engagement for this reason?
choices: The hourly rate charged by the testing firm
The vendor's uptime guarantee for its services
The names of the hospital's software suppliers
Approved testing windows and an emergency contact
questions.answer: Approved testing windows and an emergency contact
questions.explanation: Defining when testing may happen and whom to call if something breaks reduces the chance of harming critical services. The hourly rate is a commercial term for the contract or SOW, not a safety control.

questions.stem: Each quarter, the compliance team gives the executive team a dashboard showing how well each department follows the security policies and which gaps remain open. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: Reporting compliance status to the organization's own leadership is internal reporting. External reporting goes to outside parties such as regulators or business partners.

questions.stem: A merchant must send an annual report on its payment card security to its acquiring bank to confirm it meets card industry requirements. Which of the following BEST describes this report?
questions.explanation: A report delivered to an outside party to show compliance is external reporting. Internal reporting stays within the organization, for example to management or the board.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of internal compliance reporting?
choices: A breach notice sent to a data protection authority
An annual filing submitted to a banking regulator
A compliance certificate shared with a major client
A monthly report to the board on audit findings
questions.answer: A monthly report to the board on audit findings
questions.explanation: Reporting to the board keeps the organization's own leadership informed, which makes it internal. Notices to regulators and certificates for clients go to outside parties, so they are external reporting.

questions.stem: After a breach of customer data, a European company informs its national data protection authority within 72 hours, as the law requires. Which of the following BEST describes this action?
questions.explanation: Providing required information to a regulator is external compliance reporting. Internal reporting would inform the company's own management rather than an outside authority.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose of internal compliance reporting?
choices: To meet a regulator's mandatory filing deadline
To let leadership track gaps and fund remediation
To certify the company's compliance to its customers
To replace the need for external audits
questions.answer: To let leadership track gaps and fund remediation
questions.explanation: Internal reporting keeps the organization's own leaders informed so they can prioritize and fund fixes for compliance gaps. Filings to regulators and certifications for customers go to outside parties, so they are external reporting.

questions.stem: A data protection authority orders a company to pay a large monetary penalty after finding that it processed personal data without a lawful basis. Which of the following consequences of non-compliance is this?
questions.explanation: A monetary penalty imposed by a regulator is a fine. Sanctions are broader restrictions, such as bans on doing certain business, rather than a payment.

questions.stem: After a contractor repeatedly fails to meet required security controls, a government agency bars it from bidding on any government contracts for 3 years. Which of the following consequences of non-compliance BEST describes this?
questions.explanation: Restrictions imposed by an authority that limit what an organization may do, such as debarment, are sanctions. Loss of license would remove the legal authorization to operate at all, which goes further than barring contract bids.

questions.stem: News reports reveal that an online bank ignored security requirements for years. No penalty has been issued yet, but many customers close their accounts and move to competitors. Which of the following consequences of non-compliance is the bank experiencing?
questions.explanation: Loss of customer trust and business after public exposure is reputational damage. Fines would require a regulator to impose a monetary penalty, which the scenario says has not happened.

questions.stem: A logistics partner invokes a penalty clause and reduces its payments to a company because the company failed to keep the security controls promised in their agreement. Which of the following consequences of non-compliance is this?
questions.explanation: Penalties that arise from breaking the terms of an agreement are contractual impacts. A fine is imposed by a regulator or court, not by a business partner under a contract.

questions.stem: Before adopting a new cloud HR platform, the compliance team researches which regulations apply to employee data and evaluates whether the platform's controls meet them. Which of the following does this BEST demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Due diligence is the investigation done before acting to understand obligations and risks. Due care is the ongoing effort to keep protections in place after the decision is made.

questions.stem: Each new employee signs a form confirming that she has received and read the acceptable use policy. Which of the following BEST describes this signed form?
questions.explanation: An acknowledgement confirms that a person has received and understood a policy. An attestation is a formal declaration that something is true, such as required controls having been performed, which is more than confirming receipt of a document.

questions.stem: A company hires an outside firm to check, on an ongoing basis, whether its systems continue to meet the requirements of a privacy regulation. Which of the following types of compliance monitoring is this?
questions.explanation: Monitoring performed by a party outside the organization is external compliance monitoring. Internal monitoring would be done by the company's own staff, such as its compliance team.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of automating compliance monitoring?
choices: Removal of the need for any human review of the compliance results
Continuous detection of drift with less manual effort
Guaranteed passing results on every audit
questions.answer: Continuous detection of drift with less manual effort
questions.explanation: Automation checks systems frequently and flags drift quickly without relying on manual spot checks. It does not remove the need for people to review results and fix issues.

questions.stem: Under privacy regulations such as GDPR, which of the following parties is responsible for deciding the purpose of processing personal data and its lawful basis?
questions.explanation: The controller determines why and how personal data is processed and is accountable for having a lawful basis. A processor only processes the data on the controller's behalf and follows its instructions.

questions.stem: A customer asks an online store to delete all of her personal data. The store must keep her purchase invoices for 7 years under tax law. Which of the following is the BEST response?
choices: Refuse the whole request because some of her data must be kept by law
Delete the other data and explain the invoices must be kept
Keep all the data until the 7 years have passed
questions.answer: Delete the other data and explain the invoices must be kept
questions.explanation: The right to be forgotten has limits where other laws require retention, so the store should erase what it can and explain the exception. Refusing the whole request is wrong, since only the invoices are covered by the legal requirement.

questions.stem: A company stores its customer records with a SaaS provider. If the records are mishandled, which of the following parties remains primarily accountable to the customers whose data was collected?
choices: The data center hosting the SaaS service
The customers whose data it is
The company that collected the data
questions.answer: The company that collected the data
questions.explanation: The organization that collects the data and decides how it is used keeps ownership and accountability, even when another party stores it. The SaaS provider acts as a processor and has duties, but it does not take over the company's accountability.

questions.stem: A US-based company has customers in California, Brazil, and Germany. Which of the following BEST describes the privacy legal implications the company must address?
choices: Only the laws of the country where it is headquartered
State, national, and international laws may all apply
Only the laws of the state where its servers are located
Only industry standards, since privacy laws do not cross borders
questions.answer: State, national, and international laws may all apply
questions.explanation: Privacy obligations can come from local/regional, national and global laws based on where the data subjects live. Following only home-country law is the tempting mistake, since laws such as GDPR apply to companies outside the EU that serve EU residents.

questions.stem: A company's policy requires customer support chat logs to be deleted 2 years after the conversation ends. Which of the following does this requirement BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Data retention defines how long data is kept and when it must be disposed of. A data inventory records what data exists and where, but it does not set how long it is kept.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY privacy reason to keep an up-to-date data inventory?
choices: To know where personal data is stored and processed
To reduce the cost of cloud storage and backups each year
To speed up software deployments to production
To replace the need for a data retention policy
questions.answer: To know where personal data is stored and processed
questions.explanation: An inventory shows what personal data exists and where, so it can be protected and requests such as deletion can be answered. It supports a retention policy but does not replace it.

questions.stem: A company keeps every customer record indefinitely in case the data is useful someday. Which of the following is the MAIN privacy risk of this practice?
choices: Backups will take less time to complete
More personal data is exposed if a breach occurs
Customers gain more legal rights to access the stored data
Data owners lose the ability to classify data
questions.answer: More personal data is exposed if a breach occurs
questions.explanation: Holding data longer than needed increases what attackers can steal and may break retention requirements in privacy laws. Customers' access rights do not grow because data is kept longer.

questions.stem: A privacy officer finds that the marketing team copied customer data into a spreadsheet on a shared drive that is not listed in any company records. Which of the following should be updated to address this gap?
questions.explanation: The data inventory should record every location where personal data is stored, including this spreadsheet. A retention schedule sets how long data is kept, but it cannot help with data the company does not know exists.

questions.stem: The company's own audit staff reviews whether IT followed the change management policy for every production change made last quarter. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: An audit performed by the organization's own audit staff to check policy compliance is an internal audit. A regulatory examination would be carried out by a government authority.

questions.stem: To keep the internal audit function independent, to which of the following should the head of internal audit report?
choices: The audit committee of the board
questions.answer: The audit committee of the board
questions.explanation: Reporting to the audit committee keeps auditors free from pressure by the managers whose areas they audit. Reporting to the CISO would compromise independence when the auditors review security controls.

questions.stem: A company's CEO signs a formal statement to regulators certifying that the company's internal controls over financial reporting are effective. Which of the following BEST describes this statement?
questions.explanation: An attestation is a formal declaration that the stated facts about controls are true. A self-assessment is the process of reviewing one's own controls, not the signed certification of the result.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN drawback of relying only on self-assessments to evaluate security controls?
choices: They always cost more than an independent external audit would
The results may be biased by a lack of independence
They cannot be repeated more than once a year
They require the company to share source code
questions.answer: The results may be biased by a lack of independence
questions.explanation: People reviewing their own work may overlook or downplay weaknesses, so self-assessments are less objective. They are usually cheaper than external audits, not more expensive.

questions.stem: A company hires an outside consultant to compare its security program against a published framework and recommend improvements. No formal opinion or certification will be issued. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: An outside review that evaluates posture and identifies gaps is an external assessment. Attestation would require a formal opinion or declaration, which this engagement does not produce.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes how a regulatory examination differs from other external audits?
choices: It is voluntary and carried out by the company's own internal staff
It only reviews the physical security of buildings
It is required by law and done by a government authority
It is done by the vendor that sold the security tools
questions.answer: It is required by law and done by a government authority
questions.explanation: Regulatory examinations are mandated and performed by government regulators with enforcement power. The company's own staff would be performing an internal audit, not an examination.

questions.stem: A large merchant that processes millions of card payments each year must have a qualified outside assessor validate its compliance annually. Which of the following does this requirement call for?
questions.explanation: Validation by a qualified outside assessor is an independent third-party audit. A self-assessment is completed by the merchant itself and is generally allowed only for smaller merchants.

questions.stem: A company is choosing a firm to perform its external security audit. Which of the following is the MOST important quality of the audit firm?
choices: Ownership of the company's security tools
A seat on the company's steering committee
Responsibility for running the company's SOC
Independence from the company being audited
questions.answer: Independence from the company being audited
questions.explanation: An external audit is only credible if the auditor has no stake in the results. A firm that runs the company's SOC would be auditing its own work, which destroys independence.

questions.stem: A team of testers acts as attackers and tries to break into the company's systems to find weaknesses before real criminals do, without working alongside the defenders. Which of the following types of penetration testing is this?
questions.explanation: Offensive testing, often called red teaming, focuses on attacking to find exploitable weaknesses. Integrated testing would combine the attackers and defenders, sharing findings during the test.

questions.stem: During an exercise, the SOC focuses on detecting and responding to simulated attacks so it can measure how quickly it spots intrusions and contains them. Which of the following types of penetration testing does the SOC's role represent?
questions.explanation: Defensive testing, often called blue teaming, evaluates the ability to detect and respond to attacks. Offensive testing is the attacking side, not the team measuring its own detection and response.

questions.stem: A company hires testers to find out whether its locks, cameras, and security guards can stop an intruder from reaching the wiring closets on each floor. Which of the following types of penetration testing is this?
questions.explanation: Testing whether physical barriers and guards stop unauthorized entry is physical penetration testing. Offensive is a broad term for attacker-side testing, but the focus on locks, cameras and guards makes physical the best answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes integrated penetration testing?
choices: Testers receive full documentation and source code
Testers only gather public information about the target
Defenders are not told that a test is taking place
Attackers and defenders work together and share findings
questions.answer: Attackers and defenders work together and share findings
questions.explanation: Integrated testing, often called purple teaming, combines offensive and defensive teams so detection improves during the test. Receiving full documentation describes a known environment test, not integrated testing.

questions.stem: A penetration testing firm is given only the company's name and told to find a way in, with no network details, credentials, or documentation. Which of the following types of test is this?
questions.explanation: When testers start with no inside information, it is an unknown environment test. A partially known test would give them some details, such as user credentials or IP ranges.

questions.stem: A company wants a penetration test that simulates a malicious developer who already has full knowledge of the application's design, source code, and network layout. Which of the following test types BEST meets this goal?
questions.explanation: A known environment test gives testers full details such as documentation, source code and network diagrams, matching what an informed insider would have. An unknown environment test models an outsider who starts with no inside knowledge.

questions.stem: A company has a short testing window and wants the most thorough review of its application in the time available. Which of the following test types is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Giving testers full documentation, source code and credentials lets them cover the most ground without spending time on discovery. An unknown environment test spends much of its time on reconnaissance, which reduces coverage in a short window.

questions.stem: A bank wants to simulate an attacker who has stolen a regular customer's online banking login. Testers receive that customer-level login but no system documentation or administrator access. Which of the following types of test is this?
questions.explanation: Providing some information, such as a standard account, but not full details is a partially known environment test. A known environment test would include documentation, source code or administrator access.

questions.stem: A tester runs a port scan against the client's public IP addresses to identify which services are listening. Which of the following is the tester performing?
questions.explanation: Sending traffic to the target's systems to learn about them is active reconnaissance. Passive reconnaissance gathers information without directly interacting with the target.

questions.stem: A tester connects to the client's mail server and records the software name and version that the server displays in its greeting. Which of the following types of reconnaissance is this?
questions.explanation: Banner grabbing requires connecting directly to the target system, which makes it active reconnaissance. It is not passive, because the tester's connection can be seen in the server's logs.

questions.stem: A tester searches public certificate transparency logs and domain registration records to find the client's subdomains, without sending any traffic to the client. Which of the following is the tester performing?
questions.explanation: Gathering information from third-party public sources without touching the target is passive reconnaissance. Active reconnaissance would involve probing the client's systems directly, for example with a scan.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the main difference between active and passive reconnaissance?
choices: Passive interacts with the target and is more likely detected
Active uses only public sources such as social media
Active interacts with the target and is more likely detected
Passive requires written permission but active does not
questions.answer: Active interacts with the target and is more likely detected
questions.explanation: Active reconnaissance sends traffic to the target, so it can be logged and noticed. Gathering from public sources such as social media is passive reconnaissance, not active.

questions.stem: An employee reports a suspicious email using the phishing report button. Which of the following should the security team do FIRST?
choices: Send a company-wide warning about the email
Block every external sender in the email system
Analyze the message and find other recipients
questions.answer: Analyze the message and find other recipients
questions.explanation: The team should first confirm whether the message is malicious and identify who else received it, so it can remove the message and check for clicks. A company-wide warning may be needed later, but sending it before analysis may cause confusion over a harmless email.

questions.stem: An accounts payable clerk receives an email that appears to come from a regular supplier, asking to change the bank account for future payments. Which of the following is the BEST way for the clerk to verify the request?
choices: Call the supplier using a number from existing records
Reply to the email and ask for confirmation
Call the phone number listed in the email signature
Check that the email has the supplier's logo
questions.answer: Call the supplier using a number from existing records
questions.explanation: Verifying through a separate, trusted channel defeats an attacker who controls or spoofs the email. Calling the number in the signature is tempting, but the attacker may have written that number.

questions.stem: An employee regularly emails work files to her personal webmail account so she can work on them at home, even though she knows company policy forbids it. Which of the following types of anomalous behavior does this BEST represent?
questions.explanation: Knowingly bypassing policy for convenience, without intending harm, is risky behavior. It is not unintentional, because she is aware that the action breaks the rules.

questions.stem: A user who has only ever signed in from a company laptop in Chicago suddenly signs in from a server in another country and accesses payroll files she has never opened. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: Activity that breaks from a user's established pattern is unexpected behavior and should be investigated. Calling it risky would assume the user knowingly chose to break policy, which the logs do not show.

questions.stem: An employee sets a cloud folder to share with anyone who has the link, believing that the setting limits access to coworkers. Which of the following types of anomalous behavior is this?
questions.explanation: The employee did not realize the setting exposed the folder, so the behavior is unintentional. Risky behavior involves knowingly taking a shortcut that breaks policy.

questions.stem: Security training asks employees to report coworkers who talk about selling company data, show unusual interest in projects outside their role, or copy large amounts of files before leaving. Which of the following training topics does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: These warning signs point to someone inside the company who may misuse access, which is the focus of insider threat training. Situational awareness focuses on physical surroundings, such as shoulder surfing and tailgating.

questions.stem: Training encourages employees to use a company-approved credential vault, create a unique passphrase for every account, and never reuse work credentials on personal sites. Which of the following training topics is this?
questions.explanation: Guidance on creating, storing and not reusing passwords is password management. Operational security is about not revealing sensitive information, such as project names, through everyday activity.

questions.stem: Awareness training warns staff not to charge their phones with USB charging leads left in conference rooms or handed out at trade shows. Which of the following training topics does this BEST fit?
questions.explanation: Malicious cables and devices can carry malware or capture data, which falls under removable media and cables. Situational awareness is about noticing people and surroundings, not about the hardware users plug in.

questions.stem: An employee is about to badge through a secure door when a person carrying boxes and wearing no visible badge asks her to hold the door. Based on security awareness training, which of the following should she do?
choices: Hold the door since the person's hands are full
Ask the person to badge in or go to reception
Let the person in and report it later
Lend the person her own badge to use
questions.answer: Ask the person to badge in or go to reception
questions.explanation: Politely refusing and directing the person to badge in or check in stops tailgating, a common social engineering technique. Holding the door is the tempting courtesy, but it is exactly what the attacker is counting on.

questions.stem: Before any training is delivered, a company sends its first simulated phishing email to all staff to measure how many people click. Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of this simulation?
questions.explanation: The first measurement before training creates a baseline that later results can be compared against. Recurring monitoring comes afterward, when the same measurements are repeated over time.

questions.stem: Every month, the awareness team sends management a report that shows training completion, phishing click rates, and report rates compared with earlier months. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: Regular reports that track trends over time are recurring reporting. Initial reporting captures the starting point before the program has had an effect.

questions.stem: Phishing simulation results show the click rate has fallen to 3%, but almost no employees use the report button when they receive a simulated phishing email. Which of the following does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: Users ignore suspicious emails instead of reporting them
The phishing simulations are far too difficult for staff to recognize
The training program can now be discontinued
The email filter is blocking every phishing email
questions.answer: Users ignore suspicious emails instead of reporting them
questions.explanation: A low click rate with a low report rate suggests people delete or ignore suspicious messages rather than alert the security team. If the filter blocked every simulation, there would be nothing for users to click in the first place.

questions.stem: Awareness metrics show that the finance department clicks on simulated phishing emails at twice the company average. Which of the following is the BEST next step?
choices: Provide targeted training to the finance team
Remove email access from the finance team
Stop running simulations for the finance team
Repeat the same annual training for all staff
questions.answer: Provide targeted training to the finance team
questions.explanation: Using results to target the group with the highest risk is how monitoring improves the program. Repeating the same generic training for everyone ignores what the data shows.

questions.stem: Which of the following metrics would BEST show that employees are becoming more willing to alert security about suspicious messages?
questions.explanation: A higher report rate shows employees are actively reporting suspicious messages. Completion rate only shows that people finished training, not that their behavior changed.

questions.stem: A company is creating its first security awareness program. Which of the following should the team do FIRST?
choices: Buy a training platform with a large content library
Launch monthly phishing simulations for all staff
Publish training completion targets for managers
Assess the organization's risks and audience needs
questions.answer: Assess the organization's risks and audience needs
questions.explanation: Program development starts by understanding the risks and the audience so content and goals fit the organization. Buying a platform first risks choosing content that does not address the company's actual risks.

questions.stem: In a company's awareness program, developers receive secure coding training, finance staff receive training on payment fraud, and help desk staff learn to verify callers. Which of the following BEST describes this approach?
questions.explanation: Tailoring content to each group's job risks is role-based training. Generic annual training gives everyone the same content regardless of their role.

questions.stem: A company replaces its single two-hour annual awareness session with short monthly lessons and quick quizzes. Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of this change?
choices: Fewer policies for employees to acknowledge
Removal of the need for any metrics
questions.explanation: Short, frequent lessons keep security in mind and improve how much people remember. They do not replace simulations, which test whether people apply what they learned.

questions.stem: A company is planning the rollout of its security awareness program. Which of the following groups should take part?
choices: All staff, including executives and contractors
Only employees hired in the last year
Only employees who failed a simulation
questions.answer: All staff, including executives and contractors
questions.explanation: Everyone with access to company systems can be targeted, and executives are frequent targets of phishing and fraud. Limiting training to IT staff leaves most of the workforce unprepared.

questions.stem: An awareness program built three years ago still covers fax scams but has no content on QR code phishing or deepfake voice calls. Which of the following should the program owner do?
choices: Keep the content since employees know it well
Update the content to reflect current threats
Stop the program until a new vendor is chosen
Add a fourth policy acknowledgement each year
questions.answer: Update the content to reflect current threats
questions.explanation: Awareness content must be reviewed and updated as threats change so training stays relevant. Keeping familiar but outdated content leaves employees unprepared for the attacks they are most likely to face.
